title: Collecting Milkweed Seeds for Illegal Planting
source_creator: Joey Santore / Crime Pays But Botany Doesn't
primary_use: milkweed flower morphology, pollination mechanics, terminology teaching, and secondary Malvaceae morphology; source species are not assumed Hays-local

rights.public_reuse: not assumed cleared; obtain separate permission/license before publication

curation_rules: Keep only frames that visibly teach a plant, structure, diagnostic character, or field-identification concept.
Do not keep a frame merely because the narration names a structure if that structure is not visible in the image.
Treat source names and labels as source evidence; canonical taxonomy and target-zone range reconciliation occur later in the Hays Botany pipeline.
If source terminology conflicts with an independent botanical reference, do not promote the incorrect label into the canonical glossary; preserve the source discrepancy in notes.

rejected_notable_mentions.reason: Narration explains milkweed fruits, but he states developing follicles are not yet visible.
Narration and on-screen definition discuss the silky seed coma, but no actual seed/coma is shown in the frame.
Narration explains clonal shoots, but the underground/root connection is not visually demonstrated.
Ecological chemistry is discussed, but the frame does not visually demonstrate the chemical trait or exuding latex.

records.notes: Source overlay identifies Asclepias speciosa (showy milkweed) and Apocynaceae; useful habitat and whole-plant context.
Joey points directly at the large flowering umbel while beginning the milkweed-flower morphology explanation.
Close intact-flower view while Joey identifies the upright hoods and the horn-like projections inside them.
Excellent macro frame with tool tip and on-screen label pointing to the stigmatic slit.
On-screen label defines pollinium (plural pollinia) during explanation of aggregated pollen masses.
Source overlay identifies Sidalcea oregana and Malvaceae; useful whole-plant and inflorescence context.

Close flower view showing the central staminal column. The video briefly labels this structure as an androgynophore, but Flora of North America describes Sidalcea/Malvoideae as having a staminal column and explicitly states androgynophore absent; stored under the corrected term.
Joey removes part of the flower and exposes a yellow pollinium; on-screen label reads Pollinium Exposé.
Dissected macro showing the yellow pollinium connected toward the dark corpusculum while Joey explains the translator apparatus and connecting arm.
Joey points to the recurved petals immediately before reviewing the central milkweed reproductive structures.
Dissected flower with blade pointing to the central reproductive column and on-screen Gynostegium label.
Dissected flower with blade and on-screen Corona label; useful for relating the corona to the hoods around the gynostegium.
Dissected flower with on-screen Hoods label and pointer; strong terminology frame.
